title: SpotServe: Serving Generative Large Language Models on Preemptible Instances
technique: dynamic reparallelization (D,P,M,B) on spot instances, Kuhn-Munkres device mapping/migration planning, token-level stateful inference recovery within cloud grace period, mixing on-demand instances

optimized_metrics.evidence: This paper aims to reduce the monetary cost for serving LLMs by leveraging preemptible GPU instances on modern clouds
Overall, the optimizer minimizes the end-to-end inference latency l_req(C) while maintaining a throughput higher than alpha_t

C_{t+1} <- argmin_{C | phi(C) >= alpha_t} l_req(C) else C_{t+1} <- argmax_C phi(C)   [Algorithm 1: pick the lowest-latency config whose throughput phi(C) covers arrival rate alpha_t, else maximize throughput]

headline_claim.text: SpotServe can reduce the P99 tail latency by 2.4-9.1x compared with the best existing LLM serving systems. We also show that SpotServe can leverage the price advantage of preemptive instances, saving 54% monetary cost compared with only using on-demand instances.

reported_metrics.where: monetary cost vs on-demand (54% saving), Fig 7
overload (dashed lines) when serving capability < arrival rate

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For each inference request, its end-to-end inference latency l_req is divided into two parts: the scheduling overhead l_sch and the execution latency l_exe.
metric_definitions.notes: includes queueing/scheduling delay; l_exe(S_out|S_in) = t_exe(S_in) + sum_i t_exe(S_in+i) i.e. whole-request prefill+decode time (Eq. 1); no TTFT/TBT/TPOT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Taking the P99 latency as an example, SpotServe outperforms Reparallelization and Rerouting around 1.34-2.43x and 2.14-9.13x respectively on the largest LLaMA-30B model.
metric_definitions.notes: per-request end-to-end latency distribution over the trace; no explicit formula for P99 beyond percentile

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SpotServe can utilize spot instance to reduce the monetary cost for serving LLMs by up to 54% compared with the on-demand instance while preserving close average inference latency
metric_definitions.notes: dollar cost of instances (spot vs on-demand price); not per token

load_regime: trace replay of 12-hour AWS g4dn spot availability trace (two 20-min segments); stable Gamma arrivals (CV 6; 1.5/0.35/0.2 req/s for OPT-6.7B/GPT-20B/LLaMA-30B) and fluctuating MAF trace
tradeoff_acknowledged: balances throughput, latency and monetary cost; spot-only saves 54% cost at <18% higher average latency and 90% higher P99 than on-demand (abstract/§6.2); overload when preemption leaves capacity below arrival rate
hardware: AWS g4dn.12xlarge (4x NVIDIA Tesla T4 per instance), up to 16+ GPUs; built over FasterTransformer
workloads: request arrival Gamma process CV=6 (stable) and Microsoft Azure Functions trace MAF (fluctuating); input/output 512/128 tokens
extractor_notes: No TTFT/TBT/TPOT; latency is whole-request. P99 is the headline reported/optimized stat, though the algorithm's controller minimizes l_req (modeled latency) subject to a throughput covering the arrival rate. Layer coded energy/cost since the core motivation is monetary cost; could also be parallelism.
